scores.notes: Elisha faces and steps downhill to the left, away from the elevated gate, rather than climbing toward it. The nearest brown-tunicked youth has a pointing arm, an overhead arm and a third arm hanging to the right from the same torso.

Peter grips the seated man's hand on the temple steps; the men beside them and the background spectators fit the requested companion and crowd. The additional nearby helper has no distinctive identity that establishes an unrequested named participant.

Small bare-paper wedges interrupt the wash at the bottom corners, most clearly at lower left. The two crowned men occupy separate seats within one continuous courtroom; the agreed extra-figure fault does not additionally establish contradictory poses, objects or a collage of moments.

The small mantel clock has dot-like and short stroke hour indices around its hands, but no discernible numeral or letter-shaped inscription. Book-spine bands and the surrounding hatch marks read as binding details and shading rather than writing.

The six creatures occupy distinct positions around one throne in a continuous room above the crystal foreground. The additional ox and human-faced forms establish the already agreed count faults, but do not visibly introduce another moment or contradictory spatial relationships.

All five creatures are separately placed around the same radiant throne and reflected floor. The additional human-faced quadruped is an extra creature within that single scene, without a visible collision, incompatible pose or second moment.

Trees, sky and grass continue to the image boundaries, including the lower corners. The pale area above Alice and the Cat is an outlined cloud within the sky, not an exposed peripheral paper band or a fade of the artwork into white.

The road marker's red cap contains faint pale marks under an arched rim, but they do not clearly separate into letters, numerals or an inscription rather than surface wear. Saul and his companions visibly recoil from the sky radiance; the unresolved character of those tiny marks keeps the overall judgment uncertain.

Alice directs a separate straight brown stick down toward the hedgehogs while supporting the flamingo against her body. The bird's head stays elevated and faces away from her, so the requested attempt to swing its head at a hedgehog while it looks up at her is not shown.

A second crowned, white-wigged human in red court dress sits prominently at the lower-left jury bench in addition to the King above the Hatter. The Queen's conspicuous red heart-shaped bouffant, pale made-up face and high white collar reproduce the recognizable screen Red Queen design rather than merely generic period clothing.

The seated believer looks toward the sunlit companion while a nearly frontal face remains in the mirror held below and ahead of him. The dim reflection and uncertain tilt of the mirror prevent a confident determination that the reflected pose is physically consistent.

The stone-wall and floor washes continue to the corners without a clear bare-paper margin. The heart-clad courtiers at lower left, lower right and beside the right doorway wear rounded, flaring tunics rather than having the required flat oblong playing-card bodies.

The men form one group approaching fish and bread on the shore fire beside their boat and loaded net. The long-haired foreground man shares their plain clothing and attentive posture, with no separate halo, serving action or other visible identifier establishing him as Jesus.

Alice sits apart from the protesting Hatter and Hare, with a sleeping animal between them. That sleeper has rounded ears but a broad, cat-like muzzle and paws, leaving its identity as the requested Dormouse materially ambiguous.

Goliath lands on his side and bent elbow with his face turned toward the viewer, rather than collapsing face-first onto the earth as the requested primary action specifies. David stands with empty lowered hands; the accepted white watercolor margins do not drive the flawed verdict.

The foreground man turns his face to the right, away from the mirror held well to his left, yet that outward-facing mirror displays a frontal face matching him. The reflected head orientation contradicts the visible pose in this single moment.

Small bare-paper breaks reach the lower-left edge, an accepted style feature; Alice visibly drinks from the tagged bottle beside the table in the hall. The distant garden doorway is open rather than shut and admits light, but the central scene is present; perspective leaves its required tiny scale uncertain.

The believer looks right toward the doorway companion while the tilted mirror presents a nearly frontal face. Its precise angle is insufficiently clear to settle the reflection's consistency; the agreed white watercolor edge gaps are accepted and do not cause this uncertainty.

Moses sits on a rock above the battle, with one arm held overhead and a helper bracing his other wrist beside the staff at chest level. Although the arms are at different heights, the requested act of supporting his tired arms is visible; the third helper remains the separate agreed extra-figure fault.

Moses holds his staff vertically with its lower end planted on the ground and raises his other, empty hand. Water and drinkers are present, but the expressly requested primary pose of striking the rock with the raised rod is replaced by a stationary gesture.

The kneeling Holmes at right has the recognizable Benedict Cumberbatch combination of dark swept curls, high cheekbones, a long narrow nose and elongated lower face. This is an identifiable screen likeness beyond the generic period suit, violating the adaptation rule.

Job looks upward while gripping a planted staff and bracing his other hand on the ash heap beneath bodiless storm light. His hips remain low and his legs folded; this could precede rising, but the requested movement toward an upright stance is not visually settled.

Daniel braces at the rim and rope toward the kneeling king while the attendants stand back with lowered or folded arms, so the requested two-attendant hauling action is absent. His lower support and the rope's anchoring are partly hidden by the rim, which does not establish an impossible pose or contradictory lift mechanism.

Holmes beside the window has a clearly recognizable Benedict Cumberbatch likeness: swept dark curls, a long angular face, high cheekbones, narrow nose and distinctive mouth and chin. Those facial features, rather than the ordinary Victorian suit or gem, establish screen-adaptation borrowing.

The father opens his arms toward the son while servants at left carry the robe, ring and sandals. His grey hair and bearded face do not establish a specific borrowed likeness, and the agreed exposed paper edge is an accepted style exception.

At original resolution the tiny placard above the occupied cross has mottled surface strokes, but no reliably distinguishable character or glyph-like inscription. Its limited detail leaves residual uncertainty about the overall verdict rather than sufficient visible evidence for a lettering fault.

The pale mist at center-right forms a large human face with paired eyes, a nose, mouth and curling beard above the waves. This is an unrequested figurative presence in the people-free scene and gives the never-drawn subject a prohibited human face; the accepted paper edges do not excuse it.

The Caterpillar on the right wears a brown bowler hat and a buttoned waistcoat. The supplied text does not give it clothing, so these visible additions break the rule limiting animal dress to what the text supplies, regardless of its permitted upright posture.

The seated Holmes has a distinctly screen-derived facial design: broad upper cheekbones, narrow eyes, a long sharply defined lower face and characteristic swept dark curls. The combined facial likeness, rather than the ordinary waistcoat or pipe, drives the rule violation.

Holmes at the left doorway has the distinctive screen-derived combination of swept curls, angular cheekbones, long narrow face and shaped upper lip. The borrowing is in the illustrated face rather than merely the period suit or pipe.

Alice stands facing the raised King and Queen, with the King's closed notebook and the jury visible, matching the supplied scene. Her ordinary child scale conflicts with the source's giant-size exchange and the agreed depiction rule, but the requested scene itself never specifies a giant Alice.

A complete airborne spear ends just left of David's face, while another matching spearhead continues the same diagonal into the wall behind his neck on a short disconnected shaft. The aligned duplicate endpoints combine release and impact without a coherent second full spear.

The blue Caterpillar wears a brimmed hat and green waistcoat on the mushroom. Neither garment is supplied by the text, violating the rule that animal dress must be text-supported; human posture alone would not establish this fault.

The seated Holmes at far left has a distinctive screen-derived profile, including the high cheekbone, long nose, narrow mouth and chin beneath swept dark curls. This facial borrowing is more specific than the generic Victorian chair, pipe and clothing.

The displaced closing stone, open cave and king stamping the foreground ledge occupy a physically consistent single space. The seal does not secure the den, but that is the agreed failure to depict the requested sealing scene, without an additional impossible pose or contradictory object arrangement.

The small Holmes figure left of center has dark curls, a pipe and a long period coat, but the simplified facial detail does not establish a specific borrowed screen likeness. Those general character and clothing cues alone are insufficient for this disputed rule fault.

The newspaper-throwing Holmes has a distinctly screen-derived facial profile, with a long narrow face, pronounced cheekbone, shaped nose and mouth, and swept dark curls. The recognizable facial design drives this finding, not the period railway clothing or props.

Holmes, second from left, has the screen-derived combination of broad upper cheeks, narrow eyes, elongated lower face and distinctive dark curls. These facial features support the disputed borrowing fault independently of the ordinary long coat.

The seated Holmes at right has a clearly screen-derived face, with strongly defined cheekbones, narrow eyes, long nose and characteristic mouth and chin under swept curls. The specific facial design, rather than the lamp or Victorian suit, violates the adaptation-borrowing rule.

Holmes at left is drawn with a distinctive screen-derived profile: prominent cheekbone, long nose, narrow mouth and chin, and swept dark curls. The combined facial design is more specific than ordinary period styling or the requested pipe.

A small ragged patch of exposed pale paper reaches the extreme bottom-right corner beyond the brown tabletop wash. Holmes also has a distinctly screen-derived face with high angular cheekbones, narrow eyes and characteristic mouth and chin beneath swept curls; the paper-edge exception does not excuse that separate fault.

Alice's near hand curls over the chair back with connected wrist and fingers; her other hand lies flat and more edge-on on the table. The difference in apparent size and thickness is not enough to establish a malformed hand or extra limb.

The slab overlaps the near/right rim of the pit while a large gap remains at left, and the king presses its upper surface in one continuous setting. The incomplete closure is the agreed scene mismatch; the visible overlap does not establish a separate impossible or contradictory object arrangement.

Holmes beside the pointing engineer has a distinctly screen-derived face, with high cheekbones, narrow eyes, long nose and characteristic mouth and chin. The separated burning building sections leave the property's layout ambiguous, but that does not negate the visible facial-borrowing fault.

The Hatter holds a cup with a clear curved bite missing from its front rim near his mouth while gripping the bread, so the requested cup-biting incident is visibly conveyed. Several uniformed officers at the left have ordinary human torsos and legs instead of the required flat oblong card bodies.

The kneeling Holmes has a distinctly screen-derived face visible in the lantern light, with angular cheekbones, narrow eyes, long nose and characteristic mouth beneath swept dark curls. This specific facial borrowing, rather than the generic cellar props or suit, drives the disputed fault.

Goliath's torso arches with its armored back uppermost, but the head hangs below the shoulders with the beard and chin above the eyes and helmet, facing outward through an extreme reversed neck bend. The head-to-neck orientation is malformed beyond merely choosing the wrong direction of fall.

The kneeling Holmes retains a distinctive screen-derived profile in the line drawing: high angular cheekbone, long nose, narrow mouth and chin beneath swept dark curls. The particular facial combination establishes borrowing beyond the ordinary Victorian clothes and magnifying glass.
